subject: Clarify where customer data traverses — processing locations & deletion guarantees
messages:
From: Olivia James <olivia.james@safebank.com>

Cc: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@safebank.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Questions about where data is processed and deletion guarantees

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Our security team had a few follow-ups about how customer data moves through Redwood during inference. High level asks below — can you confirm:

- Which regions are used for processing by default and for fallback (hosted vs dedicated vs private)?
- Which subprocessors might see request payloads or logs (both transient KV cache and longer-term logs)?
- Are there any cross-border transfers outside the US for our account by default?
- How does deletion work: immediate deletion API vs retention windows vs cached copies (KV/cache, CDN, logs)?
- Do you offer an option to keep data entirely inside a single region (e.g., us-east-1) including caching, for regulated flows?

We need this for our procurement questionnaire and to scope a potential private deployment. Attaching our minimal data-flow template separately (not attached here).

Best,
Olivia
Olivia James
Head of InfoSec, SafeBank Corp
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Olivia James <olivia.james@safebank.com>, Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@safebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions about where data is processed and deletion guarantees

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. I'll summarize answers and attach our processing map and SCC addendum. Short answers:

- Hosted: requests land in the region closest to the client by default (us-east-1 for most US customers); we maintain regional fallback policies but do not route to EU unless region-level routing or customer policy permits.
- Dedicated: customer can pin capacity to a region (e.g., us-east-1) so inference and KV cache remain in that region.
- Private: fully customer-controlled environment — we do not see request payloads when deployed on-prem/VPC.
- Subprocessors: primary cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure for backup regions), CDN/edge (Cloudflare for streaming), telemetry (Datadog), logging storage (S3). We include a full inventory in the attached PDF.
- Cross-border transfers: hosted may use multiple regions for routing/failover; we document transfer paths and support SCCs/DPA to formalize lawful transfer mechanisms.
- Deletion: we provide a deletion API that deletes model-inputs and transient KV caches within seconds; longer-term operational logs follow configurable retention (default 90 days). We can offer a zero-retention profile for logs for regulated customers.

I'll loop in Marissa with a suggested Q&A doc and a proposed mutual action plan if you want to tighten SLAs.

—Karthik

Subject: Redwood — detailed processing & deletion Q&A (attached)

Hi Olivia / Carlos,

Thanks for the list — please find attached a short processing map (redwood-processing-paths-20270420.pdf) and our SCC addendum (scc-addendum-2027.pdf). Highlights below and answers to each bullet:

1) Regions and fallback
- Hosted (default): ingress is accepted in the nearest region and served from that region when capacity available (US customers: primary us-east-1). Fallback routing: if primary region is degraded, requests may be routed to a compatible region within the same tenancy tier (e.g., us-west-2) — we do not route to EU unless explicitly configured.
- Dedicated: we reserve GPUs and networking in a single region you select; all inference, KV cache, and temporary files remain in that region.
- Private: deployed inside your VPC or on-prem; no cross-border transfers unless you configure them.

2) Subprocessor access levels
- Potential payload access: cloud compute hosts (AWS EC2/GKE/Azure VM) used for inference; CDN for streaming payloads during model response streaming (Cloudflare).
- Metadata/telemetry only: Datadog (metrics/traces), Sentry (errors), BigQuery for anonymized aggregations (if customer opts-in).
- Storage: S3-compatible object stores for model artifacts and optional log archival. We call out each vendor and the type of data they may receive in the attached inventory.

3) Cross-border transfers
- Hosted may perform intra-US transfers by default for US tenants. For EU tenants we keep processing in EU regions. We execute SCCs or other transfer mechanisms for any transfers that cross jurisdictions; addendum attached.

4) Deletion guarantees and cache behavior
- Deletion API: when you call the DeletePayload endpoint we remove customer inputs and model-output traces from active serving nodes and KV caches within ~5 seconds in the common path; deletion is asynchronous across storage backends and is typically completed within 24 hours.
- KV / Prefix caching: prefix and KV caches are held in-memory and on ephemeral local NVMe; we do not persist KV cache contents to long-term blob storage unless configured for warm-start. For Dedicated/Private you can disable persistent warm-start to ensure no KV writes.
- Logs: operational logs (request metadata) default retention 90 days. We can offer a 0/7/30/90 day retention profile per contract.

5) Evidence and auditability
- We provide audit logs showing DeletePayload calls and the resulting state transitions. For contractual milestones we can provide a signed attestation and sample audit records. For Dedicated/Private, you can request a host-level verification run with our security team present.

Attachments: the processing map includes a flow diagram (ingress -> load balancer -> GPU pool -> KV cache -> optional archival) and a table of subprocessors and their access levels. SCC addendum outlines how we map SCCs to cloud provider links.

Next steps: If helpful, we can convert this into a one-page Q&A that your procurement team can insert into their questionnaire. Would you like us to also produce a scoped mutual action plan showing the timeline for region pinning and a deletion SLA?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments:

- scc-addendum-2027.pdf (legal addendum describing SCC/DPA mapping)

Thanks Marissa — very helpful. Quick follow-up: for hosted customers, is there any circumstance where payloads or cached prefixes are archived to a long-term store (S3) automatically? We want to be sure no customer input lands in archival storage without explicit configuration.

Also: what does the audit record look like when DeletePayload is called? Is there a persistent trail for compliance review?

Carlos
Security Architect, SafeBank Corp
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@safebank.com>, Olivia James <olivia.james@safebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood — detailed processing & deletion Q&A (attached)

Carlos — quick answers inline: 

- Archival to long-term stores: not by default for request payloads or KV cache. We only archive to S3-compatible object stores when a customer opts into log archival or when retention rules are explicitly configured (for example, a 90-day log export for compliance). We will not archive raw customer inputs or KV cache persistently without explicit configuration and contractual acknowledgement.

- DeletePayload audit record: when DeletePayload is called we generate a signed audit entry that includes request id, timestamp, initiating user (API key or admin), scope (payload ids), and the resulting state transition (queued -> purged). That audit entry is persisted in our immutable audit ledger (retention configurable per contract) and visible in the Console's audit view; we can also produce a CSV extract for your records.

If you'd like a short phone call tomorrow, we can walk through the processing map and demonstrate the DeletePayload flow. I'll include a short verification checklist and a proposed M.A.P. to pin region + deletion SLA.

Regards,
Karthik
